text:
Forensic findings
1) Domain context: In residential real estate, landlords typically manage properties through lease agreements, tenant screening files, property maintenance logs, and rent-roll spreadsheets. Ordinary controls in this field include independent pricing based on market comparables (comps), disclosure of material terms to tenants, and standard accounting records. Lease documents generally contain fields for rent amount, security deposit, term length, and occupancy date. Communication occurs through email, property management software, or in-person meetings, with standard practice maintaining independent decision-making for each property owner.

2) What occurred: The actor initiated coordinated communications with multiple competing landlords via <CHANNEL-1> (encrypted messaging) and <CHANNEL-2> (in-person meetings). The actor created <DOC-1>, a spreadsheet with columns for <LANDLORD_ID>, <NEIGHBORHOOD_ID>, <AGREED_RENT_FLOOR>, and <MARKET_SHARE_ALLOCATION>. The actor populated <DOC-1> with specific rent floor values for each geographic zone. The actor transmitted <DOC-2>, a penalty matrix listing <TENANT_ID> or <LANDLORD_ID> entries with <UNDERCUT_AMOUNT> fields, distributed to participants via <CHANNEL-1>. The actor maintained <DOC-3>, a communication log with entries timestamped <DATE>, where plaintext was replaced with coded terminology (e.g., "seasonal adjustment" for rent floor changes, "community standards" for penalty enforcement). The actor deleted <DOC-4>, prior draft versions showing iteration history, and purged <CHANNEL-1> metadata by using <TOOL-1> to re-encrypt archived messages under new keys.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor accessed <ACCOUNT> credentials for three property management systems, each holding tenant databases with <TENANT_COUNT> records. The actor used <DEVICE-1> (laptop, hostname <HOSTNAME>) and <DEVICE-2> (mobile, EID <EID>). The actor stored <DOC-1> through <DOC-4> in <STORAGE-1> (cloud drive, account <ACCOUNT>) and <STORAGE-2> (local SSD, partition <PARTITION>). The actor accessed <COMP-DB>, a third-party rent comparison database, to calibrate <AGREED_RENT_FLOOR> values.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Encrypted message threads in <CHANNEL-1> containing the coded vocabulary list from <DOC-3>. The <MARKET_SHARE_ALLOCATION> field in <DOC-1> showing non-random geographic partitioning inconsistent with organic market distribution. The <PENALTY_MATRIX> in <DOC-2> correlating temporal proximity of <UNDERCUT_AMOUNT> entries with subsequent rent increases by non-participant landlords in <NEIGHBORHOOD_ID>. Deleted-file remnants of <DOC-4> recovered from <STORAGE-2> journal logs, showing three iterations with escalating <AGREED_RENT_FLOOR> values. Metadata in <CHANNEL-2> meeting confirmations showing recurring <DATE> pattern (weekly, same time) across all participants. The <TOOL-1> re-encryption event logs showing batch key rotation occurring <TIMESTAMP> after each <CHANNEL-1> session.

5) Notes: The coded vocabulary in <DOC-3> mapped to 14 distinct operational terms. The <MARKET_SHARE_ALLOCATION> percentages in <DOC-1> sum to 100% across 6 geographic zones. The deleted drafts of <DOC-4> show the actor refining the penalty mechanism over <DURATION> before finalizing <DOC-2>.
